intro.text: A Keeper who comes to Luthadel after a message from Sazed and offers to teach Elend Venture how to be a better ruler.
A Terris Keeper and member of the Synod, tutoring Elend Venture in leadership, who stays in Luthadel to study Kwaan's inscription with Sazed.
A Keeper and member of the Terris Synod, remembered in northern Scadrial as the Mother of Terris.

items.text: Tindwyl spent much of her life in the Lord Ruler's breeding program, where she had no formal training in Feruchemy, though she was given a few copperminds and studied the biographies in them. She resented the Synod for what she endured there, and for its unwillingness to act against the Lord Ruler.

Around forty, no longer able to bear children, Tindwyl joined the Keepers. Sazed recited the Keepers' collected knowledge to her over months, and they came to know each other well. In the following ten years she rose to prominence among the Terris, becoming a senior Keeper and a member of the Synod.
Tindwyl first appeared at a meeting of Luthadel's Assembly, where Vin noticed her and pointed her out to Elend.

A few days afterward, Demoux caught Tindwyl apparently eavesdropping on Elend's meeting with the crew. Elend recognized her from the Assembly, guessed she was a Keeper sent by Sazed and agreed to see her alone. She promptly snapped her bonds, having let herself be caught while Vin was away on her rounds.

Tindwyl explained that her specialty as a Keeper was the biographies of great men, and offered to teach Elend to rule better. He accepted. When Vin burst in demanding to know why she was there, Tindwyl remarked on her directness. Her first instruction to Elend was to stop saying "um", and he had her given rooms in the palace.
Tindwyl was pleased when Demoux complimented Elend's new uniform. Discussing what makes a good king, she told Elend it was trust.

When Sazed returned to Luthadel, Tindwyl met him privately and scolded him for ignoring the Synod's orders to teach in the Eastern Dominance. They argued over his belief that something was wrong with the mists, and she wondered aloud how a man who should have led the Terris had become a rebel. Leaving, she took his hand for a moment, then shook her head and went.

Dress shopping with Vin and Allrianne, Tindwyl urged Vin to speak to the Survivor's followers gathered outside, telling her that as the Lord Ruler's killer and the king's consort she could not simply be left alone. Afterward, she lost patience with Vin's doubts and told her to decide whether she believed in the city.

Tindwyl apologized to Elend for treating him like a child and praised how quickly he learned. Talking about Vin, she told him Vin felt unworthy of him, mentioning that she had raised many daughters, and warned that he might have to choose between Vin's love and Luthadel's people.

After Elend lost his throne, Tindwyl helped write his speech to the Assembly, which tied the new government to Kelsier by putting Vin in the spotlight. She frowned when Elend did not ask for his crown back as planned.

While Elend and the others searched the law for a way to stop Cett becoming king, Tindwyl was displeased to learn Sazed had proofread it. Elend refused to let her insult Sazed and told her to apologize to him or leave. She left without a word.

Before Vin's dinner with Cett, Tindwyl complimented her gown and told her Elend hardly needed lessons anymore, since good leadership came from experience. She said he had likely been on this path all along, and that Vin's own growth was for herself as well as for Elend.

Days after Elend's last lesson, Tindwyl found Sazed among the refugees and saw that he did care for the people. At last she asked to see what had brought him running back. Taking his hand, she told him he was the kind of man her biographies praised and asked him for a reason to stay; he asked her to stay, and she did.

When Elend asked whether he had been foolish to tell the truth and lose the throne to Penrod, Tindwyl said the cause was his refusal to do anything dishonorable, and that acting on his conscience was commendable even if she disagreed. She had no answer for what he should do next.
Watching Elend leave, Tindwyl admitted she might have taught him too well, and that had the Assembly not deposed him he could have saved Luthadel. She and Sazed returned to studying the inscription.

Tindwyl's last words to Elend were harsh: she told him his people would remember him as a coward. She left him the document she and Sazed had written on the Deepness, the prophesied Hero and Kwaan's inscription, for the Synod in Tathingdwen.

Tindwyl stayed with Sazed. Embracing him, she told him she loved his strength of will and his firmness when he knew he was right, and that sending Vin, Elend and Spook away was both wrong and right. Then the warning drums began to sound.

Dockson gave Tindwyl command of Tin Gate, one of the first places the koloss struck. It fell hours into the battle, and she was killed leading her soldiers toward Keep Venture. Sazed found her body and mourned her.
In northern Scadrial, Tindwyl is remembered as the "Mother of Terris", and Tindwyl Promenade in Elendel's Fourth Octant bears her name.

appearance.text: Tindwyl is tall and lean, about fifty, with a rectangular, square-featured face and beautiful eyes. Her straight auburn hair, going gray, reaches her waist and is sometimes braided.

Tindwyl's earlobes are stretched by many earrings of alternating colors. She wears colorful Terris robes, or a bright skirt and blouse, with rings of Feruchemical metal, and her neat dress and perfect posture make her always look composed.

personality.text: Tindwyl is perceptive and quick to see what people need: firm and harsh with Elend, kind with Vin as she helps her accept herself. She often gets what she wants indirectly, coaxing Elend into accepting an honorific and into admitting how much he loves Vin.

Highly intelligent, Tindwyl shares the Keepers' love of learning and specializes in the biographies of forgotten generals, kings and emperors. Once absorbed in a task she is single-minded, staying awake for over a week to study the rubbing from the Conventical of Seran with Sazed.
Tindwyl values religion for its scholarship and its benefit to society, but is no believer, and has little patience for prophecy, foretelling or superstition.

Commanding and confident, Tindwyl orders Kelsier's crew around, to their surprise. She can seem cold, but is practical, compassionate and a romantic at heart, telling Elend that exceptions can be made for love, and she remains in Luthadel with Sazed despite her duties as a Keeper.
